subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Should OpenClaw expose resolved provider/model identity on `before_agent_run`, add a dedicated post-resolve blocking hook, or keep model-bound policy enforcement outside plugin hooks?
rationale: This changes a public plugin security boundary for policy enforcement, and the safe contract depends on maintainer intent around sanitized metadata, raw provider hooks, and backward-compatible hook semantics.

options.title: Add read-only identity to `before_agent_run`
options.body: Expose resolved provider/model metadata on the existing fail-closed blocking hook so policy plugins can enforce before model input without a new raw provider-call surface.

options.title: Add a post-resolve blocking hook
options.body: Create a new hook between model resolution and provider dispatch if maintainers want a cleaner phase boundary than extending `before_agent_run`.

options.title: Keep enforcement outside hooks
options.body: Document config-derived agent-chain or provider-selection policy as the supported enforcement path and leave hook attribution observe-only.

recommendation.title: Add read-only identity to `before_agent_run`
recommendation.body: Expose resolved provider/model metadata on the existing fail-closed blocking hook so policy plugins can enforce before model input without a new raw provider-call surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses public plugin API and security posture, and this handle is the strongest current-main routing signal from recent merged hook/runtime history.
